name: exe.dev

facts.value: Hosted standalone VMs (sandboxes) with separately reserved vCPU and memory
facts.notes: An active subscription is required: Personal starts at $15/month; Work is $75/month with a restricted first-subscription intro. Work and Enterprise standalone creation is off until an admin enables admins-only or all-users. Legacy Individual and Team plans do not include standalone VMs. These are not shared-capacity pool VMs.

facts.value: No documented support found in the official sources reviewed as of 2026-10-08 for customer-installed standalone VM runtime/control plane
facts.notes: Conservative documented-support audit classification, not a vendor denial. Reviewed docs/marketing/API and public Bold Software repositories. Open guest images, agents, SSH clients and the execonnect private-service tunnel do not establish self-hosting the sandbox service; exedev-flue describes a private exe.dev server. Enterprise BYOC is separately listed, not a public self-host installer. Search scope is recorded in the dated official-source review

facts.value: Bring your own cloud is listed for Enterprise only
facts.notes: Pricing explicitly excludes BYOC on Personal/Work and lists AWS/GCP VPC support for Enterprise. Exact standalone execution/control-plane placement, cloud coverage and contract access are not established. The official execonnect daemon tunnels private services to hosted workloads; it does not establish running the sandbox in the customer's cloud. Conditional positive support is retained, not treated as a public-plan entitlement.

facts.value: TypeScript source connector for Flue; no general standalone lifecycle SDK established
facts.notes: The official exedev-flue connector uses SSH/SFTP for a supplied VM host. Its auto-create/clone helpers issue new/cp without --standalone, so they do not establish standalone creation by default. API explorer Python/JavaScript/Go examples are direct HTTP, not SDKs. The Python exe-ssh project is an experimental interactive terminal client, not a Python sandbox SDK; execonnect is a Go private-service connector, not a Go sandbox SDK.

The reviewed official sources do not name community standalone-VM SDKs. That source omission does not establish that community clients do not exist; retain unknown until a positive community-client example or an explicit scoped negative is verified. Official first-party client and integration scope is recorded separately in the dated official-source review

facts.value: POST https://exe.dev/exec
facts.notes: The body is the same command you would type over SSH, and JSON output is always enabled. Bearer tokens are generated with ssh-key generate-api-key. The request body limit is 64KB.

facts.value: ssh exe.dev
facts.notes: Commands include new, rm, cp, resize, restart, ls, stat, share, and pool. --sandbox is an alias for --standalone. The old cli-*.md references redirect to the API explorer; its command-tree artifact is dated 2026-08-21 and omits newer standalone flags, so current standalone docs govern those flags.

facts.value: Whatever the VM image can run
facts.notes: The default image is exeuntu. new --image accepts other container images, including the example ubuntu:22.04. The how-it-works page says you do not choose the kernel.

facts.value: VM on Cloud Hypervisor, described as an implementation detail that may change
facts.notes: The VM starts from a container image plus a block device, on bare metal that exe.dev rents. VMs in one account are isolated from each other.

facts.value: Default exeuntu is Ubuntu 24.04; other Linux container images are accepted
facts.notes: The Dockerfile uses ubuntu:24.04, and the API tour offers ubuntu:22.04. The guest kernel is not selectable; this is not arbitrary kernel/Windows VM support. Image architecture limits are not specified.

facts.value: Standalone default 2 vCPUs; maximum 16 on Personal and 32 on Work
facts.notes: Enterprise limits are custom. new --cpu and resize --cpu configure guest allocation. The 512 vCPU ceiling and approval above 32 vCPU refer to shared Work pools, not an individual standalone VM.

facts.value: Standalone default 2 vCPUs / 8 GiB; maximum 32 GiB on Personal and 64 GiB on Work
facts.notes: Current pricing explicitly uses GiB. The metered capacity unit is 2 vCPU / 4 GiB; the default-size row is 2 vCPU / 8 GiB. How independently sized CPU and memory map to billable units is not explained; do not infer a default VM bill. CLI examples and the Personal capacity doc still use GB; no conversion was made. Pool maxima are not standalone maxima.

facts.value: --disk accepts sizes such as 50GB; resize only grows the VM disk
facts.notes: The disk-usage FAQ meters used ext4 filesystem space, not simply provisioned size, and describes exeuntu as about 4 GB. A production standalone disk default or maximum was not established; the explorer's 20 GB default is simulated. Pricing includes 100 GiB per 2 vCPU; billing docs still say 100 GB. Disk allowances are not disk-size maxima and units were not converted.

facts.value: No documented support found in the official sources reviewed as of 2026-10-08 for GPUs inside standalone VMs
facts.notes: Conservative documented-support audit classification, not an explicit vendor denial. Current standalone sizing/pricing, docs index, custom-image/runtime references, public client artifacts and GPU-targeted searches establish CPU VMs but no GPU allocation mechanism, hardware or access tier. Enterprise custom resource limits and nested virtualization are not GPU support.

facts.value: new --image boots a VM from a published Docker/container image, including private registries
facts.notes: Custom images are included on current plans. --registry-auth=USERNAME:PASSWORD supplies host-side boot pull credentials; integration hostnames are unavailable before the VM exists. In-guest registry integrations are separate. exe.dev/login-user sets the SSH user. Guest kernel selection, image architecture/size limits, build/preparation charges and readiness timing are not established by this mechanism.

facts.value: Install packages over SSH with guest privileges or bake them into a custom image
facts.notes: exeuntu runs /exe.dev/setup once at first boot. The explorer command-tree reference specifies a 10KiB setup-script maximum; use indirection. Setup completion is not included in a measured readiness claim.

facts.value: Guest root access; default exeuntu user exedev has passwordless sudo
facts.notes: The homepage says SSH users are root; exeuntu's Dockerfile actually configures login-user=exedev and exedev ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL. Custom images can select a different login user. This is guest privilege, not host/root access to exe.dev infrastructure; share --root is a collaborator access level.

facts.value: Docker runs inside the VM
facts.notes: The Docker FAQ shows docker run on the exeuntu image. Nested virtualization (KVM) is marked included on Enterprise and not included on Personal or Work.

facts.value: Detached processes and systemd/cron workloads can keep running in the VM
facts.notes: The HTTPS guide detaches with setsid nohup and writes /tmp/build.log. /exec has a 30-second request timeout, not a 30-second VM lifetime. The 2026-03-03 persistence post says lack of traffic/SSH does not quiesce VMs. A running idle standalone VM retains reserved-capacity billing; stopping retains disk, not documented process memory.

facts.value: scp, rsync, ssh and SFTP
facts.notes: The copy-files FAQ documents SSH-based transfer, and the official Flue connector implements SFTP reads/writes. The HTTPS example cats a file through /exec; its request limits are separate from SSH/SFTP. Transfer/export is not a VM snapshot or post-delete restore guarantee.

facts.value: Persistent VM disk survives guest reboot and stop/restart
facts.notes: Stopped standalone VMs keep their disk and count toward limits. rm deletes the VM; no post-delete restore or retention guarantee is established. cp captures files into a new VM. Regional NVMe replication is described as a backup a few seconds behind the source, not zero-loss recovery, a user snapshot API, or process-memory preservation. Separate attachable volumes are unverified.

facts.value: No documented support found in the official sources reviewed as of 2026-10-08 for separate attachable standalone VM volumes
facts.notes: Audit documented-support inference, not vendor denial. Persistent root disks, cp disk clones, regional disk replication and S3 integrations are different mechanisms. Docs/marketing/storage/API and public-repository searches did not establish volume create/attach/detach support; search ledger is in the dated official-source review

facts.value: Disk-preserving guest stop and restart, not established memory-preserving pause
facts.notes: The pools marketing page documents ssh <vm>.exe.xyz sudo poweroff, then ssh exe.dev restart <vm> to boot the same disk. It separately confirms stopped standalone VMs keep disk and incur no vCPU/memory billing, matching standalone docs. They still consume VM slots; retained disk can incur storage charges and subscription continues. No hibernate/live-resume API is established.

facts.value: No documented support found in the official sources reviewed as of 2026-10-08 for standalone VM process-memory snapshots or live resume
facts.notes: Audit documented-support inference, not vendor denial. poweroff/restart boots the same disk; cp copies disk/configuration. Neither establishes RAM capture. Idle persistence is not a suspend/resume transition. Experimental exe-ssh named terminal sessions reconnect after a dropped client link, not VM poweroff/replacement. Lifecycle, marketing, API and official source rechecks found no VM memory-save/restore mechanism.

facts.value: Filesystem cloning via cp: copy-on-write disk capture into a new VM
facts.notes: The 2026-02-08 January Update describes copy-on-write cp; the current API tour says it duplicates the whole disk. cp --standalone is documented. This supports file cloning, not RAM capture, a named snapshot/restore API, or restore after source deletion. Application consistency, retention, clone disk accounting and separate snapshot/clone fees are not specified. Custom boot images are a different mechanism.

facts.value: cp copies an existing VM's disk into a new VM, including cp --standalone
facts.notes: Copy-on-write is documented; the command-tree reference offers CPU, memory, disk and copy-tags options. New standalone copies reserve their own capacity and are subject to plan/creation gates and VM limits. Do not infer process-memory forking, an in-place reset operation, application-consistent snapshots, or free clone storage.

facts.value: Outbound bandwidth is metered
facts.notes: Outbound is any traffic that leaves exe.dev. Inbound does not count toward the allowance.

facts.value: Default all egress; optional integrations-only outbound policy
facts.notes: Enable the account feature yourself with defaults write dev.exe feature.egress-policy true, then egress <vm> integrations. This blocks public internet but retains metadata and attached integration endpoints; it is not deny-all. New VMs use DNS 169.254.169.254; older VMs need manual resolv.conf configuration. HTTP integrations can target configured services, but arbitrary domain/IP/CIDR rules, protocol/port coverage, DNS/SNI enforcement and bypass resistance are not established. No blanket network-isolation guarantee.

facts.value: Vendor HTTPS proxy to a service inside the VM; no dedicated VM public IP
facts.notes: EXPOSE prefers port 80, otherwise the smallest exposed TCP port >=1024; share port changes target. Default exeuntu exposes 8000 and 9999. HTTPS ports 3000-9999 are private to authorized users; only one selected service port can be public. This is HTTP(S) proxying, not arbitrary raw TCP/UDP or a caller-machine tunnel. SSH is separately brokered. Team admins can restrict public/external sharing. The migration guide permits localhost:8000.

facts.value: https://vmname.exe.xyz/ reaches the VM's configured HTTP service through managed TLS
facts.notes: Private by default with exe.dev login; share set-public exposes one selected port, subject to team sharing policy. VM-scoped bearer tokens support programmatic private access; X-Exedev-Authorization is preferred, Authorization deprecated. Endpoint availability depends on the VM/service running. General sharing docs describe collaborator access, but pricing marks Personal Sharing / Access controls not included; Personal collaborator-sharing entitlement remains conflicting, not a reason to negate documented HTTPS service ingress.

facts.value: No general inter-VM private network per FAQ; scoped peer HTTPS and external private-service connectors; Enterprise AWS/GCP VPC listed
facts.notes: VM-to-VM integrations proxy to authorized target VMs, not private IP routing. Official execonnect source documents outbound-only tunnels from private services to authorized exe.dev workloads, with published TCP/HTTP/HTTPS endpoints; it does not move VM execution into the caller's cloud or establish public VM ingress. Its setup UI requires login, so public-plan availability and standalone applicability remain unresolved. Enterprise VPC/BYOC topology is unverified; Tailscale is user-installed.

facts.value: Standalone VM count limits: 50 on Personal, 100 on Work, Enterprise custom
facts.notes: Stopped standalone VMs still count. Personal caps all VMs at 50. Work pool limits (25 VMs per vCPU, up to 1,000 per pool) are not standalone concurrency. No separate simultaneous-exec or numeric creation-rate limit is established; HTTPS requests have per-SSH-key 429 throttling without a published quota.

No numeric standalone VM lifetime maximum was established after lifecycle/API/marketing rechecks; do not infer unlimited. Running VMs bill reserved capacity while waiting or idle. /exec has a separate 30-second request timeout, with detached work documented. rm deletes the VM; stopped VMs keep disk and consume a slot without compute billing.

No numeric standalone idle timer was established. The 2026-03-03 persistence post explicitly says no quiescing merely for absent traffic/SSH. Current standalone docs meter reserved capacity while running, not active CPU only. Stopped VMs are a separate state. Search-discovered devbox/usage-pricing pages returned 404; their stale autosleep/per-second snippets are not current standalone evidence.

facts.value: HTTP 429 when one SSH key sends too many requests
facts.notes: No numeric quota was printed. The limit is per key.

facts.value: LAX, NYC, DAL, FRA, TYO, SYD, SGP, and LON accept new placement; PDX does not accept new accounts
facts.notes: Each account has a region. Pool VMs use the pool's region. The lobby is in the United States. Personal pool placement is the user's region. Work can place a pool in any region.

facts.value: Interactive SSH output and an experimental HTTPS/WebSocket terminal client
facts.notes: Official exe-ssh source streams terminal output messages over the VM xterm WebSocket endpoint and reconnects named shells after client-network drops. It is explicitly experimental, requires an interactive local TTY and does not establish VM memory snapshots. POST /exec separately documents combined stdout/stderr plus X-Exe-Exit, no stdin/PTY and a 30-second timeout; its incremental-output guarantees are not established. Do not infer them from served-app SSE support.

facts.value: Command output in /exec; guest log files; stat VM metrics
facts.notes: The detached-work example writes /tmp/build.log. stat ranges are 24h, 7d, 30d; these are metric windows, not an application-log retention promise. No separate managed application-log retention/export SLA was established.

facts.value: SSH, and a browser terminal for Root collaborators
facts.notes: The HTTPS /exec API explicitly has no PTY.

facts.value: Attached integrations store credentials server-side and inject them at the network edge
facts.notes: VM processes use attached service endpoints without receiving durable integration credentials; HTTP proxy integrations inject headers and S3 integrations sign requests. This is service-scoped secret mediation, not an established arbitrary guest-secret vault/injection API. new --env is ordinary VM environment configuration, not managed secrets. Boot --registry-auth is separate; token permissions JSON is plaintext and must not contain secrets.

facts.value: API token command permissions, VM proxy authentication, Web/Root sharing and team roles
facts.notes: Token cmds limits command names, generally not arguments; ssh <vm> can restrict VM command execution. Default tokens do not grant every lifecycle command and there is no built-in nonce/replay protection. Root collaboration grants guest SSH/Terminal/Shelley, not host access. Team standalone creation is off until an admin enables it; admins may restrict external/public sharing. Pricing marks Personal Sharing / Access controls not included while general sharing docs give no plan gate; Personal collaborator-sharing entitlement is unresolved.

facts.value: Shelley, MCP at https://exe.dev/mcp, default-image coding agents and official TypeScript Flue connector
facts.notes: new --prompt requires Shelley in the image. exeuntu includes Shelley at port 9999; the Running Agents guide names preinstalled claude, codex and pi. Other images need their own agents. MCP authenticates through the browser. Flue supports an existing standalone VM host over SSH/SFTP, but its auto new/cp helpers omit --standalone. Agent/model access is separate from resource billing; current plans include no recurring monthly Shelley credit.

facts.value: Apache-2.0 for the exeuntu image repository
facts.notes: The LICENSE file in github.com/boldsoftware/exeuntu is Apache License 2.0, copyright 2026 Bold Software, Inc. The hosted service is not that file.

network_isolation.note: Default egress is all. Self-enable the account egress-policy flag and choose integrations to block public internet but retain metadata and attached integrations. Older VMs require DNS configuration at 169.254.169.254. Protocol/port enforcement and bypass resistance are not specified; HTTPS/SSH ingress remains separately controlled.

egress_allowlist.note: Opt-in integrations policy permits metadata and attached integration endpoints while blocking public internet. HTTP proxy integrations can target configured services. This is restricted service-mediated access, not an established arbitrary domain/IP/CIDR allowlist or deny-all mechanism; omission of those rules is not proof they are unsupported.

inbound_ports_or_preview_urls.note: Vendor-managed HTTPS reaches an in-VM HTTP service at https://vmname.exe.xyz/. Private by default; one chosen port can be public subject to team policy. Alternate HTTPS ports 3000-9999 stay private; VM tokens authenticate private callers. Not arbitrary raw TCP/UDP or a caller-machine tunnel.

private_networking.note: No general inter-VM private network per FAQ; scoped peer HTTPS exists. Official execonnect source tunnels private TCP/HTTP/HTTPS services to authorized exe workloads, not sandbox execution into BYOC or general public VM ingress. Setup UI is login-gated; exact standalone/public-plan availability and Enterprise VPC topology remain unresolved.

snapshots.note: cp captures the VM disk as a copy-on-write new VM and cp --standalone is documented. File cloning, not process-memory capture or a named snapshot/restore API. Application consistency, post-delete retention and clone storage accounting/fees are unverified.

memory_snapshot_or_live_resume.note: No documented support found in the official sources reviewed as of 2026-10-08 for VM RAM/process snapshots or live resume. Audit inference, not vendor denial. cp and poweroff/restart retain files only as documented; exe-ssh reconnection preserves a still-running terminal shell, not VM memory across stop/replacement. See the audit search ledger.

pause_resume.note: Documented guest sudo poweroff followed by lobby restart boots from the same disk. Stopped standalone VMs incur no vCPU/memory billing, but retain disk, consume a slot and retain subscription/storage obligations. This is stop/start, not documented hibernate/live memory resume.

cloning_forking.note: cp is a copy-on-write copy of an existing VM, and cp --standalone makes the copy a standalone VM.

persistent_filesystem.note: VM disk survives reboot and stop/restart. rm deletes the VM; post-delete restore is unverified. Regional disk backups lag by a few seconds, not zero-loss guarantees; cp can clone files into a new VM.

volumes.note: No documented support found in the official sources reviewed as of 2026-10-08 for separate attachable volumes. Audit inference, not vendor denial; persistent root disk, replication, cp and S3 integrations are not volume attachment. See the audit storage/API search ledger.

custom_images.note: new --image accepts a container image, including a private registry with --registry-auth, and the pricing table marks custom Docker images included.

docker_in_sandbox.note: The Docker FAQ says the exeuntu image can run docker run.

root_sudo.note: Guest root is advertised; default exeuntu login user exedev has passwordless sudo in its Dockerfile. Custom-image login user is configurable. This is not root access to the exe.dev host or control plane.

gpu.note: No documented support found in the official sources reviewed as of 2026-10-08 for GPUs inside standalone VMs. Audit documented-support inference, not vendor denial; Enterprise custom limits/nested VMs do not establish GPU allocation. See the audit search ledger.

self_hosted.note: No documented support found in the official sources reviewed as of 2026-10-08 for a customer-installed standalone VM runtime/control plane. Audit inference, not vendor denial. Public guest/client/agent/external-service connector code is not self-hosting the private exe.dev server; Enterprise BYOC is distinct. See the audit ledger.

byoc.note: BYOC is listed Enterprise-only, explicitly excluded on Personal/Work. Standalone execution/control-plane placement and cloud/contract access details are unresolved. execonnect private-service tunnels are not customer-cloud sandbox execution.

open_source.note: The exeuntu image repository LICENSE is Apache-2.0, copyright 2026 Bold Software, Inc., and that file is not the hosted service.

background_processes.note: The HTTPS example detaches a command with setsid nohup, while the /exec call itself returns when the command finishes or hits 30 seconds.

terminal_pty.note: SSH and a browser terminal for Root collaborators exist, and the HTTPS /exec API explicitly has no PTY.

command_streaming.note: SSH interactive output and official experimental exe-ssh HTTPS/WebSocket terminal streaming are evidenced. exe-ssh requires a local TTY and reconnects still-running named shells. /exec incremental-output guarantees remain unverified and it has no stdin/PTY with a 30-second timeout; do not generalize terminal behavior to that API.

secrets_management.note: Integration credentials are stored server-side and injected/signed at the network edge for attached service endpoints. Ordinary --env is not managed secrets; arbitrary guest secret-vault injection is unverified, and token permissions JSON must not contain secrets.

python_sdk.note: No documented support found in the official sources reviewed as of 2026-10-08 for a Python standalone VM SDK. Audit inference, not vendor denial: stdlib HTTP examples and the experimental Python exe-ssh terminal client are not a sandbox SDK. Official repo/API search scope is in the audit ledger.

typescript_sdk.note: Official TypeScript Flue connector source can operate a supplied standalone VM host over SSH/SFTP. Its automatic new/cp helpers do not pass --standalone, so they default to ordinary placement rather than establish standalone lifecycle SDK support. Direct JavaScript fetch examples are not a SDK.

go_sdk.note: No documented support found in the official sources reviewed as of 2026-10-08 for a Go standalone VM SDK. Audit inference, not vendor denial: net/http examples, the Flue prompt-serving handler and execonnect private-service connector are not a sandbox lifecycle SDK. See the audit official-repository/API ledger.

cli.note: Lifecycle commands run over ssh exe.dev, and --sandbox is an alias for --standalone.

mcp_or_agent_integrations.note: MCP at https://exe.dev/mcp, image-dependent Shelley/new --prompt, and an official TypeScript Flue connector. Flue's auto-create/clone helpers omit --standalone; a supplied existing standalone host is the scoped path. These are agents/clients, not self-hosted sandbox servers.

max_vcpu.note: The standalone max size is 32 vCPUs on Work and 16 vCPUs on Personal; Enterprise is Custom, and the 512 vCPU figure is a pool size.

max_memory_gib.note: Current pricing explicitly publishes a standalone maximum of 64 GiB on Work and 32 GiB on Personal; Enterprise is custom. This is not a GB-to-GiB conversion or the pool maximum. Personal capacity/CLI docs still use GB separately.

max_session_duration_seconds.note: A standalone VM is billed by the hour while it runs, and no maximum lifetime was printed.

idle_timeout_seconds.note: The standalone page does not describe an idle shutdown.

pricing_summary: An active subscription is compulsory: Personal $15/$35/$75/$155 per month, with standalone compute additional; Work $75/month includes 2 vCPU + 4 GiB across pools and standalone VMs, with eligible first-team subscriptions $37.50/month for 3 months. Standalone reserved capacity is $0.105 per 2 vCPU / 4 GiB unit-hour while running, not active-CPU consumption. Stopped VMs keep disk and incur no vCPU/memory charges but retain storage/subscription obligations. Extra used disk is $0.08/GiB/month averaged over the cycle; extra outbound bandwidth is $0.05/GiB, not a monthly bandwidth rate; inbound does not count. Allowance docs still use GB while pricing uses GiB. Default size is 2 vCPU / 8 GiB, so its mapping to 2 vCPU / 4 GiB billing units remains unverified, as do minimum rounding increments and unlisted creation/image/clone/I/O charges. Enterprise is contract-priced; dated September launch pricing differs from current Work docs.

pricing.conditions: Compulsory active subscription, prepaid monthly. Personal doc capacities are 2/4/8/16 vCPU with 4/8/16/32 GB memory and 100/200/400/800 GB disk; 200 GB outbound and 50 total VMs. Current pricing labels corresponding memory/disk/bandwidth GiB; the unit conflict is not converted. Included pool compute is shared, but standalone compute is charged additionally. No recurring monthly Shelley credit.

Whole-team base subscription, prepaid, includes 2 vCPU + 4 GiB across pools and standalone VMs together; no per-seat fee. Intro applies once per team billing account with no past subscription, including canceled Work or legacy Team; canceling does not restart it. Usage, disk, bandwidth, credits and taxes are not discounted. The 2026-09-28 launch post still says $150 minimum with 4 vCPU / 8 GB; current billing docs and pricing agree on $75 and 2 vCPU + 4 GiB, but existing-account transition terms are not established.
Contract pricing. Pool capacity, standalone VMs, disk, and bandwidth are covered by the contract. Dedicated hardware is listed.

Reserved capacity billed while running, including waiting/idle and I/O time; not measured active CPU. Personal pays on top of subscription; Work includes 2 vCPU + 4 GiB across pools and standalone VMs together. Vendor example is a 2 vCPU VM running 10 hours costing $1.05, without stating its RAM. Default-size row says 2 vCPU / 8 GiB; independently sized CPU/RAM mapping and sub-hour rounding/minimum are not explained. Stopped VMs incur no vCPU/memory billing, keep disk and consume slots; subscription and retained disk remain relevant. rm deletes VM and capacity. No invented workload bill.

pricing.published_price: Default 2 vCPUs / 8 GiB memory (size, not a separate charge)
pricing.conditions: Maximum 16 vCPUs / 32 GiB on Personal and 32 vCPUs / 64 GiB on Work; Enterprise custom. Standalone VM limits 50/100/custom. Pool ceilings do not apply to each standalone VM. The metered unit is 2 vCPU / 4 GiB, not the default size; no default-size bill inferred.

Average extra used storage over the monthly billing cycle, not peak or simply provisioned capacity. FAQ measures ext4 filesystem usage and notes periodic fstrim; exeuntu itself is about 4 GB. Stopped VMs retain disk, not free storage. Allowance docs still say GB while current pricing uses GiB; no conversion. Clone sharing/deduplication accounting and snapshot retention fees are unverified.

Extra outbound traffic accumulated over the billing cycle, measured in GiB (1,073,741,824 bytes). Inbound does not count. This is a per-data-volume rate, not $/GiB/month. Allowance docs use GB and pricing uses GiB; allowances are not silently converted. Metered usage is billed when the plan renews.

pricing.published_price: Docs: 100 GB disk per 2 vCPU and 50 GB bandwidth per vCPU; pricing: corresponding GiB
pricing.conditions: Disk allowance averaged over billing period; bandwidth per billing period prorated by capacity lifetime. A running standalone VM carries its own size-based allowance, unlike a VM sharing a pool's allowance. Allowances do not transfer between pools; stopped standalone allowance details are not further specified. Personal instead shares its account allowance, including a flat 200 GB in docs / 200 GiB on pricing. Units conflict; no normalization.

pricing.published_price: Hourly reserved compute; separate creation/build/clone/storage-I/O fees and minimum rounding increment not specified
pricing.conditions: The official rate is per unit-hour, but sources do not establish a one-hour minimum or per-second rounding. No separate published CPU-only/RAM-only standalone rates, image build/pull/preparation, creation/reset/clone, snapshot or storage-I/O fees were verified; missing prices are not free. Current homepage/blog navigation says by the second, but /sandbox now redirects to hourly standalone docs and /usage-pricing returns 404; old usage-pricing snippets are not a current offer. Enterprise contract terms are separate.

performance_claims.conditions: Vendor-reported generic VM creation from a container image plus block device; FAQ has no publication date, percentile, hardware, region, image cache, cold/warm definition or standalone-specific measurement. Does not establish dependency/setup completion, command readiness, reset, clone or resume latency. API tour separately says roughly a second; illustrative VPS outputs show 0.8s/0.6s. These are not a unified benchmark.

Vendor January Update published 2026-02-08: copy-on-write cp of a configured base VM into a new VM. No percentile, image/disk size, resources, cache state or region specified. Predates the 2026-09-28 standalone launch; current docs establish cp --standalone, not a standalone-specific latency test. Not memory fork, in-place reset or resume.

Marketing command-output example on the Enterprise production/pool page, undated and not an independent benchmark or standalone-specific SLA. No statistic, VM resources, disk size, region, cache conditions or application-readiness boundary specified. Do not substitute for cold creation or resume latency.

research_notes: Current pricing uses GiB for standalone memory, disk and bandwidth and publishes $0.05/GiB outbound, not per month. Personal/Work allowance docs retain GB. Default standalone 2 vCPU / 8 GiB differs from the 2 vCPU / 4 GiB billing unit. Exact sizing-to-unit mapping and sub-hour rounding remain unresolved; no workload bill invented.

Disk persistence, cp copy-on-write file cloning and guest poweroff/restart are documented. They do not establish process-memory snapshots/live resume, separate attachable volumes, post-delete restore or zero-loss infrastructure recovery. Replicated disk backup may lag a few seconds. Clone consistency, retention and storage accounting remain unverified.

Egress all is default. The account can self-enable egress-policy and use integrations-only, retaining metadata/attached services; older VMs need DNS configuration. Arbitrary domain/IP/CIDR rules, protocol/port enforcement and bypass resistance are unverified. Ingress is vendor HTTPS proxying, not raw TCP or a caller tunnel. Enterprise VPC/BYOC topology is not established.

Old cli-*.md sources redirect to the API explorer. Its command-tree artifact says generated 2026-08-21 and omits newer standalone flags; current standalone docs take precedence. Search-discovered devbox and usage-pricing pages return 404; snippets suggesting autosleep/peak-consumption/per-second pricing were not adopted. Homepage navigation still says by the second while the live standalone page says hourly; minimum rounding is unknown.

Guest sudo is verified in exeuntu's Dockerfile, not inferred from share --root. Managed integration credentials are service-scoped and held off-VM; --env is ordinary environment configuration. General sharing docs and Personal's pricing entitlement conflict. Official source recheck found TypeScript Flue connector support (existing VM only for this product), experimental exe-ssh terminal streaming, and execonnect external private-service tunnels with login-gated availability; none implies self-hosted sandbox execution or VM memory restore.
